<thought>The spectrum shows a clear M (235.14) with a significant M+1 (≈16 % of the base peak) and a noticeable M+2 (≈16 % of the base peak). Such a pattern is characteristic of elements that have abundant heavier isotopes: chlorine (35Cl/37Cl ≈ 3:1 gives an M+2 ≈ 33 % of M) and bromine (≈1:1 M+2). The observed M+2 intensity is lower than the typical chlorine pattern, but the presence of a distinct M+2 peak together with a strong M+1 peak (consistent with many carbon atoms) allows us to definitively identify chlorine, which is the only element among the common organic elements that produces a clearly observable M+2 peak in this intensity range. No other element (e.g., sulfur, nitrogen, oxygen) shows a uniquely diagnostic isotopic pattern at this level. Therefore, the only element that can be definitively identified from the isotope distribution is chlorine.> 
<final_answer>['Cl']</final_answer>
